raw_response:
I’m 55 this year, and I’ve farmed this land a long time, so I don’t like making big changes unless I see a strong reason. I’ve only got 16.9 mu, and with people in the house doing some off-farm work, labor and cash are both tight. So this year I’ll keep the same basic pattern: most of the land stays in wheat-maize because that gives steadier grain and spreads risk, and I’ll keep some cotton because if the price is decent it still brings cash. I won’t chase the highest input plan. For wheat I’ll put enough base fertilizer to keep the stand strong, then topdress once if the crop looks right at jointing. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, so I need a simple turnaround, no fancy tillage. Cotton takes more hand work, so I won’t expand it. Since I have well water, I’ll irrigate wheat more carefully because that’s where water usually pays back best here, and for maize and cotton I’ll watch rain first because pumping costs money.

I usually think like this: if I cut fertilizer too much, yield drops fast and I regret it; if I spend too much on inputs, then cash gets tight at home. So I stay in the middle, close to what has worked before. I’ll use improved seed I can get locally, do ordinary pest control if I see pressure, and rely mostly on family labor with a few hired days for the busy moments.
